twists.title: Flood on School Street
twists.situation: Heavy rain floods the road to a school. Children need to get home. Some parents want the school closed for a whole week.

options.title: Send buses on the high road
Close the school for a week
Ask parents what they want
Wait for the water to go down

twists.why: Keep children safe and moving without shutting everything.

twists.title: The Broken Shop Window
twists.situation: After a football match, a shop window is broken. People blame the visiting team's fans. The fans say they did nothing.

options.title: Ban the visiting fans from town
Check the shop's camera first
Ask both fan clubs to meet
Do nothing, it is only glass

twists.why: Find out what really happened before blaming a whole group.

twists.title: Stones at Sports Day
twists.situation: At the town sports day, two men throw stones at the runners. Everyone else in the crowd is cheering peacefully.

options.title: Send the whole crowd home
Ask the crowd to calm down
Remove only the two stone throwers
Stop the races and wait

twists.why: Stop the people doing harm. Peaceful fans can stay and cheer.

twists.title: The Late Band Practice
twists.situation: A school band practises late every evening. Neighbours are cross, and some want the band shut down.

options.title: Ban the band from playing
Measure the noise at night
Ignore it for now
Meet the band and neighbours together

twists.why: Talking together can find a practice time that works for everyone.

twists.title: Punish the Whole Class?
twists.situation: A window in Class 4 is broken. Nobody says who did it. Is it fair to punish the whole class?

options.title: No, find out who did it first
Yes, everyone gets punished
Yes, if the teacher is cross
Punish the children sitting nearest

twists.why: Punish only the person who did wrong, after finding out who it was.

twists.title: Crowd at the Cricket Final
twists.situation: A big crowd waits outside the cricket ground. The gates opened late, and people at the front are being squeezed.

options.title: Cancel the match right now
Open more gates and guide the lines
Tell people to be patient
Find out who opened the gates late

twists.why: First keep people safe and moving. Questions can wait until later.

twists.title: The Missing Library Books
twists.situation: Many books are missing from the town library. A man on the radio says the night guard took them. Nobody has checked.

options.title: Fire the night guard today
Tell readers you are looking into it
Check the library's lending records
Wait for the books to come back

twists.why: A radio claim is not proof. Check the records before blaming anyone.

twists.title: Fake Medicine at the Fair
twists.situation: A stall at the village fair sells fake medicine. Tests prove it is only chalk. Children have been buying it.

options.title: Close every stall at the fair
Put up a warning sign
Test more stalls before acting
Stop the seller and take the medicine

twists.why: The tests prove it. Stop this seller, and let the fair go on.

twists.title: The Footbridge Repair
twists.situation: The footbridge to the school will close for repairs next week. Families who walk that way are worried and confused.

options.title: Explain the plan and safe route
Say nothing until it is done
Delete worried posts about the bridge
Send guards to keep people away

twists.why: When people know the plan and the safe route, they worry less.

twists.title: Hear Both Sides
twists.situation: Two neighbours argue about a tree that drops leaves. The street leader listens to only one of them, then decides. Is that fair?

options.title: Yes, the first one is right
No, both neighbours should be heard
Only if the leader is busy
Yes, if one neighbour is older

twists.why: A fair decision listens to both sides before choosing.

twists.title: The Reporter at the Funfair
twists.situation: A reporter films a broken ride at the beach funfair. The ride owner's helpers try to grab her camera.

options.title: Ban cameras at the funfair
Ask the owner to say sorry
Keep the reporter and camera safe
Wait and see what she writes

twists.why: Reporters must be safe to show problems, so the ride gets fixed.

twists.title: The Broken Swings
twists.situation: Two swings at the park broke on the same day. A post says the new paint made the chains weak.

options.title: Close every park in town
Ask the painters to explain
Tape off the swings and wait
Test the paint and the chains

twists.why: Test what really broke before blaming the paint or closing every park.

twists.title: Fake Tickets at the Zoo
twists.situation: A man sells fake tickets at the zoo gate. Guards have filmed him three times. Families lose money every day.

options.title: Stop him and call the police
Close the zoo gate for a week
Ask him nicely to leave
Wait for him to stop

twists.why: The film proves it. Stop the one person cheating, and keep the zoo open.

twists.title: Two Teams, One Field
twists.situation: Two youth teams both want the park field on Sunday. Nobody booked it. Their coaches are arguing loudly.

options.title: Ban both teams from the park
Help the coaches share the day
Call the police to clear the field
Let them sort it out alone

twists.why: Nobody booked the field. Sharing fairly beats fighting or banning.

twists.title: A Message Is Not Proof
twists.situation: A message says the fruit seller uses false scales. Nobody has checked. Should his cart be taken away today?

options.title: Yes, the message says so
Yes, and every fruit cart too
No, check his scales first
Yes, if many people forward it

twists.why: A message is not proof. Check before you punish anyone.

twists.title: Power Cut at the Clinic
twists.situation: A storm cuts the power to a small clinic at night. A newborn baby needs a warm room.

options.title: Close the clinic until morning
Wait for the lines to be fixed
Tell everyone to stay calm
Send the generator truck to the clinic

twists.why: First help the baby stay warm. Fixing blame can come later.

twists.title: Who Won the Cycle Race?
twists.situation: At the school cycle race, one parent says the winner took a short cut. The winner says she rode the whole track.

options.title: Ask the marshals and check photos
Take her medal away now
Give both riders a medal
Wait until everyone forgets

twists.why: Hear the marshals and see the photos before taking anything away.

twists.title: The Speeding Truck
twists.situation: A truck speeds past the school every morning. The road camera has its number plate. Children cross there.

options.title: Ban all trucks from town
Stop the truck and fine the driver
Ask drivers to slow down
Wait to see if it happens again

twists.why: One driver is the danger. Stop that driver, not every truck.

twists.title: The New Pool Rule
twists.situation: The town pool now needs swim caps. Many families did not know, and they are cross at the gate.

options.title: Close the pool until people calm down
Let guards turn people away
Explain why, and start next week
Say nothing and wait

twists.why: Explain the new rule and give people time. Then most will follow it.

twists.title: Grandparents With Signs
twists.situation: Some grandparents want to walk slowly through the park with signs asking for more benches. Is it fair to stop them?

options.title: Yes, signs are not allowed
Yes, if someone dislikes benches
Only if they pay a fee
No, peaceful people may gather and ask

twists.why: People can gather peacefully to ask for things, while keeping others safe.

twists.title: The Farmers' Lake Walk
twists.situation: Farmers want to walk peacefully by the lake to ask for fair prices. They told the town office. Joggers say the path will be busy.

options.title: Let them walk, and guide the joggers
Stop the walk to keep paths free
Ask farmers to walk next month
Count how many joggers use the path

twists.why: Peaceful people can gather. Help everyone share the path.

twists.title: Tickets That Will Not Scan
twists.situation: At the ferry, many tickets sold today will not scan. The ticket seller says the machine broke. A passenger says he is cheating.

options.title: Hold the ticket seller right now
Check the machine and the records
Stop the ferry for the day
Let everyone ride free today

twists.why: Check the machine and records first. Then you know who did wrong, if anyone.

twists.title: Pushing at the Book Fair
twists.situation: Three men push people at the book fair gate and break the queue barrier. Guards saw exactly who did it.

options.title: Close the gate for everyone
Ask everyone to line up again
Move the three men away
Find out who built the barrier

twists.why: Guards saw who did it. Move just them, and let the line move on.

twists.title: The Wider Footpath
twists.situation: The town plans a wider footpath outside the shops. Shopkeepers fear they will lose customers while the work goes on.

options.title: Start digging tonight, no questions
Drop the footpath plan
Count how many people walk there
Ask shopkeepers to help plan it

twists.why: When people help plan the work, it goes better for everyone.

twists.title: The Coach's Nephew
twists.situation: The coach's nephew misses practice but still plays every match. Other players who miss practice must sit out. Is that fair?

options.title: No, the same rule for everyone
Yes, he is family
Yes, if he is the best player
Yes, if the coach says so

twists.why: Fair rules work the same for everyone, whoever they know.

twists.title: Lost at the Kite Festival
twists.situation: A small girl is lost at the kite festival. Her family is scared. Thousands of people are on the field.

options.title: Stop the festival and search everyone
Set up a help desk and announce
Question the kite sellers
Wait for her to come back

twists.why: Help the family fast, without scaring or stopping the whole crowd.

twists.title: The Science Fair Prize
twists.situation: A judge at the science fair is the winner's uncle. Other children say the prize was unfair.

options.title: Cancel all the science fair prizes
Tell the children to accept it
Ask other judges to look again
Wait for the complaints to stop

twists.why: A fair second look settles the doubt. Cancelling hurts every child.

twists.title: The Bike Lock Cutter
twists.situation: Bikes keep vanishing at the station. The camera clearly shows the same man cutting the locks.

options.title: Search every bag at the station
Ask riders to buy better locks
Watch the camera for more days
Find and stop the man on camera

twists.why: The camera shows who did it. Stop him, not every rider.

twists.title: The Very Late Train
twists.situation: A train will be three hours late. People on the platform are getting cross, because nobody tells them anything.

options.title: Tell people the real time and why
Clear the platform of waiting people
Find out who caused the delay
Say nothing until it arrives

twists.why: Honest news calms people down. Silence makes them guess and worry.

twists.title: The School Paper
twists.situation: A girl writes in the school paper that lunch is often cold. The cook wants the article taken down. Is that fair?

options.title: Yes, it hurt the cook's feelings
No, she may share honest views
Yes, only good news is allowed
Yes, if the head teacher agrees

twists.why: People may share honest views. Fix the cold lunch instead of hiding the article.

twists.title: Tell Him Why
twists.situation: A boy is told he cannot go on the class trip. Nobody tells him why, and he cannot explain his side. Is that fair?

options.title: Yes, adults always know best
Yes, if he was noisy once
No, he should hear why and reply
Yes, if the bus is nearly full

twists.why: Before a punishment, people should hear the reason and get to explain.
